events.description: Abu Muhammad al-Masri and his daughter Miriam were shot dead in a Tehran suburb by two Israeli assassins on a motorcycle, reportedly at US behest; the date was the anniversary of the 1998 embassy bombings.
The New York Times confirmed Masri's killing about a week and a half before Thanksgiving 2020, and said he had lived in Iran for five-plus years.
Al-Qaeda bombings of US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania; Masri and Saif al-Adel are implicated.
Masri, Saif al-Adel and three other senior al-Qaeda figures were released from Iranian detention in exchange for an Iranian diplomat kidnapped by AQAP; several then went to Syria and were killed.
The CIA released most of the bin Laden files, including Hamza bin Laden's wedding video filmed in Iran, reported by Long War Journal.
Wedding of Hamza bin Laden to Masri's daughter Miriam, held in Iran; date not stated, and the video was released in 2017.
White House confirmed Hamza bin Laden's death.
Mullah Omar died; Taliban and al-Qaeda hid it for over two years.
Nasir al-Wuhayshi, named in the al-Qaeda succession letters, was killed.
The head of As-Sahab was killed by Afghan forces in Afghanistan.
Acting Defense Secretary Chris Miller said only one al-Qaeda leader was left, Zawahiri.
Online rumors that Zawahiri had died of natural causes or COVID; unconfirmed.
An HTS official leaked on Telegram al-Qaeda Shura Council succession letters that placed Masri in the line of succession; the letters predate June 2015.
Khalid Islambouli assassinated Egyptian President Anwar Sadat.
Osama bin Laden killed; Zawahiri took over, and predictions of al-Qaeda's collapse did not come true.
AQIS head Asim Umar killed.
AQAP emir Qasim al-Raymi killed and replaced by Khalid Batarfi.
US-Taliban agreement signed, described by hosts as a withdrawal deal.
AQIM emir Abdelmalek Droukdel killed in early June. The hosts' 'Abdulman-Lyghild' is probably this person.
AQIM names Abu Ubaydah Yusuf al-Anabi as new emir, more than five months after Droukdel's death.
Taliban suicide attack on a base in Ghazni City housing commandos; about 30 Afghan soldiers reportedly killed.
Taliban suicide attack in Kalat targeted the head of the provincial council. Attacks in Baghlan killed a brigade commander and in Badghis a district governor.
US troop level due to fall to about 2,500 by January 2021, forcing Biden to choose among nullifying the deal, full withdrawal or a troop increase.
Taliban killed a brigade commander in Baghlan.
Taliban killed a district governor in Badghis.

Chris Miller's September statements on al-Qaeda leaders
key_claims: The hosts argue that al-Qaeda is an international organization with a general command, management committee and Shura Council, and that its branches are 'theaters of jihad' rather than loose affiliates.
Al-Qaeda's succession letters stipulate that the new leader must be in Khorasan or one of its regional branches, not just Afghanistan-Pakistan.
The hosts reject the idea that killing one or two leaders such as Zawahiri would collapse al-Qaeda, citing a deep bench including Saif al-Adel, Abd al-Rahman al-Maghrebi and Hamza al-Ghamdi.
A series of senior leaders was killed in 2019-2020: Asim Umar, Qasim al-Raymi, Droukdel, Abu Muhammad al-Masri, and the As Sahab head.
AQIM named Abu Ubaydah Yusuf al-Anabi as emir, as the hosts had predicted, after an unexplained delay of more than five months.
The hosts say al-Qaeda is replacing its first generation with a second, as bin Laden's files show him planning, and that 'silent commanders' are overlooked.
The hosts say the bin Laden files show he was an active manager, and ask who now plays Atiyah Abd al-Rahman's role for Zawahiri.
The hosts say the Taliban is escalating suicide attacks despite the Doha deal, leaving Biden three poor options: nullify the deal, withdraw fully, or add troops.
The Taliban has stepped up attacks on Afghan forces, including suicide attacks and assassinations of officials, despite the US-Taliban agreement.
The incoming Biden administration has three options: remain at ~2,500 troops (nullifying the agreement), withdraw fully, or increase troops, the last judged politically unviable.
Afghan commandos, the best-trained force, are misused as quick reaction forces and are a prime Taliban target.
The Taliban could take one or two provincial capitals, particularly in the south, if they wished, and are holding back for now.
2020 has been a good year for killing senior al-Qaeda leaders, though not enough or quick enough in the hosts' view.
